extracted.intended_audience: active lobbying registrants, in-house lobbyists, lobbying firms, and compliance officers responsible for LDA filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for registrants on complying with the Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA) and Honest Leadership and Open Government Act reporting and registration requirements, including who must register, numeric thresholds, required forms (LD-1/LD-2, LD-203), filing deadlines, amendment rules, and electronic filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly Activity Reporting Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995, as amended, requires all active registrants to file quarterly activity reports with the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives and Secretary of the U.S. Senate (LD-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly reports cover specific calendar periods and are due on fixed dates: First Quarter (Jan 1–Mar 31) due April 20; Second Quarter (Apr 1–Jun 30) due July 20; Third Quarter (Jul 1–Sep 30) due October 20; Fourth Quarter (Oct 1–Dec 31) due January 20. If the deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the report is due the following business day. Filers should use the LD-2/quarterly reporting procedures described in the official guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-Annual Contribution Reporting (LD-203) Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Honest Leadership and Open Government Act of 2007 requires active lobbying registrants and individual lobbyists to file a semi-annual report of certain contributions (LD-203) along with certification that the filer understands the gift and travel rules of both the House and Senate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribution reports are due by July 30 (for Jan 1–Jun 30) and January 30 (for Jul 1–Dec 31), or the next business day if those dates fall on a weekend/holiday. Registrants, and each of their lobbyists who were active for all or part of the semi-annual reporting period, must file separate reports detailing certain FECA contributions, honorary contributions, Presidential Inaugural Committee contributions, Presidential Library contributions, and certain payments for event costs. Filers must certify they understand House and Senate gift/travel rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Thresholds (Who Must Register)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemption thresholds specify when a lobbying firm or organization employing in-house lobbyists is required to register under the LDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective January 1, 2025: a lobbying firm whose total income for matters related to lobbying activities on behalf of a client does not exceed or is not expected to exceed $3,500 in the quarterly period is not required to register with respect to that client. An organization employing in-house lobbyists whose total expenses in connection with lobbying activities do not exceed and are not expected to exceed $16,000 in the quarterly period is not required to be registered. Section 4(a)(3) of the LDA provides that registration threshold dollar amounts be adjusted every four years based on changes in the Consumer Price Index (next adjustment shown as Jan 1, 2029). Historical threshold values and prior updates are listed in the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: JACK Act (Justice Against Corruption on K Street) Disclosure Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments from the JACK Act require additional disclosure on registrations and quarterly reports for listed lobbyists with certain criminal convictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any listed lobbyist who was convicted in a Federal or State court of an offense involving bribery, extortion, embezzlement, an illegal kickback, tax evasion, fraud, a conflict of interest, making a false statement, perjury, or money laundering, filers must include the date of the conviction and a description of the offense on LD-1 and LD-2 filings submitted after Jan 3, 2019. If statutory timelines require filing before the amended forms are available, filers should file and then amend the filing to include the relevant information once the forms/systems allow it. The office will provide technical changes and additional guidance when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing and Form Transition Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The official online filing system (LDWeb/LDWebBeta) is the required means for filing LD-1 and LD-2 disclosures; legacy IBM forms were discontinued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IBM form was discontinued after January 20, 2015. All lobbying LD-1 and LD-2 disclosures can be filed at https://lda.congress.gov/LDWebBeta. Filing online requires logging into the system using your Senate ID and password and following on-screen prompts to select filing year and type of report. The guidance encourages transitioning to the web-based forms and notes that older IBM forms will no longer be accepted after specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing System Account, Authentication, and Form Pre-population
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contributions Reporting system and other LD electronic filing tools use authenticated user accounts and provide pre-populated data to filers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to the Contributions Reporting system is based on current LDA registrations and reports with the House and Senate. Each filer signs in with a User ID and password. The system provides automated retrieval of lobbyist ID numbers and passwords, pre-populated forms containing appropriate ID numbers, names, and contact information, and requires lobbyist name verification by the employer before an individual lobbyist can create a unique password. All communications regarding filing and account status are automated and sent to the address on file. Filings can be saved, retrieved, appended, or amended after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment Procedures and Timely Amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Filers must amend registrations or reports when necessary to include newly required information or to correct filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statutory changes (e.g., JACK Act) require information not yet supported in the system, filers should submit the required registration or quarterly report on time and then amend the filing to include the relevant information once the system is updated. Notices clarify the impact of filing amended LD-1 or LD-2 reports on the duty to file an LD-203, and the Clerk’s office has issued PDFs/notice documents clarifying amendment conditions; filers should consult those notices and the Guidance for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Content: Listing Lobbyists, Affiliates, and Covered Officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance requires specific content elements in registration and reporting forms, including listing lobbyists, affiliates, and disclosures regarding covered officials and past governmental employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions to guidance include new/clarified sections regarding listing lobbyists and listing affiliates, definitions of covered officials, and additional disclosure of past governmental employment as a covered official (per Sections noted in revisions). Filers should follow the Guidance sections (e.g., Section 3 Definitions; Section 4 Lobbying Registration; Section 6 Quarterly Reporting of Lobbying Activities; Section 7 Semiannual Reporting of Certain Contributions; Section 8 Termination; Section 10 Public Availability) for exact content and format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Deadlines Summary (calendar quick reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published quick-reference of filing deadlines for quarterly activity reports and contribution reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly Activity Reports: April 20 (1st Qtr), July 20 (2nd Qtr), October 20 (3rd Qtr), January 20 (4th Qtr). Contribution Reports: July 30 (Mid Year, Jan–Jun), January 30 (Year End, Jul–Dec). If a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, the report is due the following business day. Use these dates for planning and to avoid referrals for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support, Training, and Help Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: House and Senate offices provide support, training materials, and contact points for electronic filing and account issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features and support include an online help manual, demonstrations accessible from each screen, training available on DVD and online, a written User Manual, a Troubleshooting Guide, and FAQs. Contacts: House Legislative Resource Center (202-226-5200; lobbyinfo@mail.house.gov) and Senate Office of Public Records (202-224-0758; lobby@sec.senate.gov) for help with electronic filing, registrant IDs, and passwords.

rubrics_metrics.name: LD-203 System and Process Details
rubrics_metrics.description: The LD-203 Contributions Reporting system provides a pre-populated, authenticated workflow to file required semi-annual contribution reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective June 30, 2008 the LD-203 system provides access to a pre-populated contribution form for each filer. Access is based on existing LDA registrations; filers sign in with the same ID/password used for other lobbying disclosure filings. The system enables creating a new filing for a reporting period, updating contact information, saving and retrieving filings to append before filing or to amend after filing, and a streamlined single-button submit to file with both House and Senate. All filer communications are automated and sent via email to the address on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Disclosure and Search Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Public-facing search tools and archives are provided to review lobbying disclosure and contribution filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides Public Disclosure Search, Lobbying Disclosure/Contributions Search, and a Registrant Search to locate registrant information and filings. A Forms Archive exists for past semiannual and quarterly forms and earlier versions during transition periods—consult the Forms and Software page for archives and historical forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination Reporting (Termination of a Lobbyist/Registrant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance includes rules and procedures for reporting termination of individual lobbyists and termination of registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised Guidance has a Section 8 addressing Termination of a Lobbyist/Termination of a Registrant. Filers should consult Section 8 in the Guidance for required steps, timing, and form fields to properly report terminations and to understand the effects on related filings (including whether amendments or additional reports are required).
